text: The Endangered Species Act establishes a legal framework for conserving species and ecosystems that are at risk of extinction. Its primary legal implication is that federal agencies must consult with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service or the National Marine Fisheries Service to ensure that any actions they authorize, fund, or carry out do not jeopardize the continued existence of any listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of designated critical habitat. This requirement serves as a safeguard to prevent federal activities from contributing to the extinction of protected wildlife and plants.
